title: LEGO's top-selling themes for early 2026 revealed, with Speed Champions in surprise form
summary: LEGO's official half-year financial results show Speed Champions has broken into the top five best-selling themes, pushing out long-running favourite City.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
The LEGO Group has published its official financial results for the first half of 2026, which include a breakdown of the year's best-performing themes so far. The confirmed top five are Speed Champions, Botanicals, Technic, Icons and Star Wars.

That's a notable shift from the same period last year, when City, Technic, Botanicals, Icons and Star Wars made up the top five. This time, City has dropped out entirely, replaced by Speed Champions — a theme not typically seen among LEGO's biggest sellers.

The strong showing for Speed Champions is being linked to a busy first half of 2026, with a run of new releases including movie tie-in models like the Lightning McQueen set and the Back to the Future Time Machine. Notably, none of this year's Speed Champions sets so far have been double-vehicle packs, keeping every release under £25/$30/€30. A newer release, the Jaguar F-TYPE Project 7 & Land Rover Defender Classic, launched in August and so isn't reflected in these half-year figures.

## Why it matters
This is official confirmation from LEGO's own financial reporting, giving fans a rare, data-backed look at which themes are actually resonating with buyers rather than just generating online buzz. For collectors and Speed Champions fans in particular, it's a signal the theme is having a genuine breakout moment, which could influence future set counts, pricing and licensing decisions.

## What to watch next
It'll be worth watching whether Speed Champions maintains this momentum into the second half of 2026, and whether City's dip is a temporary blip or part of a longer trend. Fans should also keep an eye on how upcoming Speed Champions releases, like the recently launched Jaguar/Land Rover set, perform once full-year figures are published.

title: Next LEGO Modular Building: Straight or Corner? The Pattern Points One Way
summary: With a fresh rumour naming 11391 Clock Tower as the 2027 LEGO Modular Building, fans have spotted a clear pattern in the collection's history of straight and corner entries.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A new **rumour** suggests the next LEGO Modular Building, tipped for 2027 and the collection's 20th anniversary, could be 11391 Clock Tower — reportedly featuring 3,264 pieces and a $249.99 price tag. Nothing here is official yet, so treat the set number, name and price as unconfirmed.

What's more interesting is the pattern fans have spotted looking back at every Modular Building since 2007. The sets seem to follow a consistent rhythm: two straight-street buildings, then a corner entry, then back to straights again. Following 2025's 10350 Tudor Corner and 2026's 11371 Shopping Street (both fitting the pattern), the next release in the sequence would logically be a straight building.

That creates an interesting wrinkle — the rumoured 'Clock Tower' name doesn't obviously suggest either shape, but going purely by the historical pattern, a straight module looks like the smart bet for 2027.

## Why it matters
The LEGO Modular Buildings Collection is one of the most popular ongoing lines for AFOLs, and spotting patterns like this helps fans predict what's coming and plan their display shelves and budgets ahead of time. For anyone building a full modular street, knowing whether to expect a straight or corner piece next year is genuinely useful for layout planning.

## What to watch next
As this is currently just a rumour, keep an eye out for any official LEGO announcement confirming (or denying) 11391 Clock Tower, its piece count, and price. Until then, the straight-vs-corner pattern remains the best clue fans have.

bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics reports that Amazon UK is currently offering a hefty discount on 75192 Millennium Falcon, the Ultimate Collector Series LEGO Star Wars set, cutting the price from £734.99 down to £578.99 — a saving of over £150.

The set has been on shelves for nine years and has an official scheduled retirement of December 2026, though that date could still shift. As the year progresses, an extension looks increasingly unlikely, and stock may run out before the retirement date even arrives.

**Rumour:** according to Brick Fanatics, there's talk of a new UCS Millennium Falcon launching in October 2027. No official details have been confirmed by LEGO, but the site speculates that, following recent trends (such as the new UCS Death Star), a replacement could come with a significantly higher price tag — potentially around £899.99.

## Why it matters
For collectors and Star Wars fans, this could be one of the last chances to grab 75192 at a discount before it's retired for good. If the rumoured 2027 version does land at a much higher price, today's deal may look like great value in hindsight. It's also a reminder that UCS sets tend to become sought-after (and pricier) once retired.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye on official LEGO retirement confirmations for 75192 as December 2026 approaches, and treat the 2027 UCS Millennium Falcon rumour with caution until LEGO makes any official announcement.

title: LEGO Insiders update lets you redeem multiple rewards in one order
summary: LEGO has simplified its Insiders rewards scheme, letting members add physical rewards straight to their basket and redeem up to three per order instead of placing separate orders each time.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has confirmed an update to its Insiders rewards programme that makes redeeming physical rewards much simpler. Previously, redeeming points for a physical reward meant generating a code and entering it separately at checkout, with only one reward allowed per order.

Now, physical rewards can be added directly to your basket just like a normal set, with points deducted instead of currency. Members can redeem up to three physical rewards in a single order, rather than needing multiple separate orders as before.

Some rewards will still have individual limits, but this change removes the need to place several orders just to grab a couple of items, such as pairing a smaller reward with a poster or similar extra. Non-physical rewards and sweepstakes are unaffected and still use the old code-based redemption method, so any codes you're holding onto can still be used as normal. LEGO says the update is already live on LEGO.com.

## Why it matters
For UK collectors who regularly stack up Insiders points, this is a genuinely useful quality-of-life change. It cuts down on postage costs from multiple deliveries, saves time at checkout, and makes it easier to combine smaller rewards into one tidy order alongside a normal LEGO purchase.

## What to watch next
Worth keeping an eye on whether individual reward limits change over time, and whether LEGO expands this basket-based system to cover sweepstakes or digital rewards in future updates.

title: Mattel Brick Shop unveils 3,500-piece adult Xbox set
summary: Mattel's brick-building arm has officially revealed a life-sized original Xbox console model with lights, sounds and hidden game dioramas, aimed at adult builders.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Mattel Brick Shop has officially announced a 3,509-piece adult building set recreating the original Xbox console at 1:1 scale, marking 25 years since the console's debut. Aimed at builders aged 17+, the set will retail for £295 in the UK and $329.99 in the US.

The model includes a full-size console and controller, plus an interior featuring diorama scenes from three classic Xbox titles: Psychonauts, Halo Combat Evolved and The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind. It also has light and sound features, with the controller's face buttons triggering different sequences tied to the games, including original soundtracks, and a hidden button combination unlocking an exclusive lighting sequence. Twelve small 'NanoWorld' figures populate the interior scenes, similar to those used in Mattel Brick Shop's Castle Grayskull set.

This follows Mattel's existing licensing deals with Microsoft, having previously released Halo-themed sets, alongside other adult-focused ranges like Masters of the Universe.

## Why it matters
This is a notable move for compatible brick brands, showing Mattel Brick Shop continuing to target adult builders with premium licensed sets and tech-integrated features like sound and lighting. For LEGO fans hoping for an official LEGO Xbox, this set effectively takes that gap in the market, especially as LEGO already covers Nintendo, Atari and Sega consoles.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for a release date and further details on the interior scenes, as well as any response from LEGO regarding console-themed sets, including the rumoured PlayStation set said to be coming later this year.

title: LEGO Icons' Spooky Midnight Valley Collection Skips the Backstory
summary: An early look at LEGO Icons 11383 Mayor Manor, the first set in the new Midnight Valley Collection, shows LEGO has deliberately left out any set lore - letting builders imagine their own story.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
A YouTuber, MiniSuperHeroesToday, has picked up an early copy of LEGO Icons 11383 Mayor Manor from a US Kohl's store ahead of its official release next month, and posted a full review. The set is the launch piece in LEGO's new Midnight Valley Collection, described as a spooky annual series in the same vein as the Winter Village Collection. It's a 1,420-piece build that comes with three glow-in-the-dark minifigures.

What's notable is what's missing: unlike story-driven predecessors such as Hidden Side and Monster Fighters, there are no named characters or explained plot. LEGO's own product page keeps things deliberately vague, describing the Midnight Valley Collection as featuring 'distorted and asymmetrical constructions' that 'create a haunting atmosphere', aimed at fans of mystery and suspense rather than a set storyline.

The reviewer says this ambiguity is intentional and enjoyable, comparing it to classic LEGO Castle sets from years past, where minimal lore left plenty of room for kids' (and now adults') own imagination.

## Why it matters
For UK fans and collectors, this signals a shift in how LEGO Icons approaches its adult-targeted seasonal collections - leaning on atmosphere and building experience rather than spelled-out narratives. If Midnight Valley follows the Winter Village model, it could become a recurring annual release worth watching for future additions and possible expansion sets.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for the official UK release date and pricing for 11383 Mayor Manor, plus whether LEGO reveals further Midnight Valley sets to build out the collection in future years.

The Barstow Sheriff's Department says a deputy spotted an abandoned van packed with large boxes and recovered the stolen sets on Monday. BNSF Railway confirmed the boxes contained the missing LEGO sets and thanked the deputy for the find.

No suspects have been named and the investigation is ongoing, with these thefts reportedly linked to a wider string of cargo train burglaries in the area.
